question_text: A 24-year-old male with cystic fibrosis is brought to the emergency room by his mother after he had difficulty breathing. He previously received a lung transplant 6 months ago and was able to recover quickly from the operation. He is compliant with all of his medications and had been doing well with no major complaints until 2 weeks ago when he began to experience shortness of breath. Exam reveals a decreased FEV1/FVC ratio and biopsy reveals lymphocytic infiltration. Which of the following components is present in the airway zone characteristically affected by the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

            ### Question
            A 24-year-old male with cystic fibrosis is brought to the emergency room by his mother after he had difficulty breathing. He previously received a lung transplant 6 months ago and was able to recover quickly from the operation. He is compliant with all of his medications and had been doing well with no major complaints until 2 weeks ago when he began to experience shortness of breath. Exam reveals a decreased FEV1/FVC ratio and biopsy reveals lymphocytic infiltration. Which of the following components is present in the airway zone characteristically affected by the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

            ### Options
    opa. Cartilage
opb. Goblet cells
opc. Pseudostratified columnar cells
opd. Simple cuboidal cells
ope. Stratified cuboidal cells

            ### Instructions:
            - Keep steps simple, each step just one state or outcome.
            - '->' separates each step.

            ### Output Format:
            Start each chain with "CHAIN:" on a new line.
            Example:
            CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "decreased blood glucose" -> "improved metabolic state" -> 90%

response:
CHAIN: Cystic fibrosis -> airway obstruction -> difficulty breathing -> 80%
CHAIN: Lung transplant -> immunosuppressive medications -> lymphocytic infiltration -> 70%
CHAIN: Decreased FEV1/FVC ratio -> obstructive lung disease -> difficulty breathing -> 90%
CHAIN: Lymphocytic infiltration -> inflammation -> airway narrowing -> 75%
CHAIN: Airway narrowing -> affects pseudostratified columnar cells -> difficulty breathing -> 85%
